stories.title: Haiti’s hunger crisis is projected to deepen
stories.summary: The IPC estimates that 5.94 million people face crisis-level hunger or worse during September 2026–February 2027. Its projection rises to 6.35 million for March–June 2027. Insecurity, displacement, high food prices and climate shocks are driving the outlook.
stories.context: The later figure is a forecast, not a current headcount. Food access and support for farming families both deserve attention.
stories.metricLabel: people projected to face acute hunger, March–June 2027

stories.title: Sudan’s damaged power network puts essential care at risk
stories.summary: The UN says strikes on Sudan’s energy infrastructure are disrupting water and hospital care. Its nearly $2.9 billion humanitarian appeal was 47% funded on November 4.
stories.context: Watch the consequences for essential services and aid access.

stories.title: Fighting in eastern Congo is closing classrooms
stories.summary: The UN reports that fighting in Uvira territory has closed 26 primary schools, affecting nearly 6,000 children. Violence is also displacing families and obstructing aid.
stories.context: Education is one of the lasting costs of conflict.
stories.metricLabel: primary schools closed in Uvira, according to the UN

stories.title: Climate preparedness faces a major funding shortfall
stories.summary: UNEP estimates developing countries will need about $305 billion a year for climate adaptation by 2035. Even the ambition to triple international public adaptation finance would cover only 20–29% of estimated needs, the agency says.
stories.context: For small island states and other exposed communities, the next question is how funding commitments become practical protection.
stories.metricLabel: estimated annual adaptation needs in developing countries by 2035

stories.title: Millions of children remain outside formal education
stories.summary: UNICEF and UNESCO report that 53% of primary-school-age children in Afghanistan are outside formal general education. Their report also says more than 2.6 million girls have been denied secondary education since 2021.
stories.context: Community learning offers some access, but the agencies say it cannot replace the right to formal schooling.
stories.metricLabel: of primary-school-age children outside formal general education

stories.title: Displacement and rising prices squeeze families in Yemen
stories.summary: The UN reports nearly 310,000 people displaced in Yemen since early August. Disrupted transport has driven up prices in Taiz; many families still need shelter.
stories.context: Food, shelter and safe delivery routes deserve sustained attention.
stories.metricLabel: people displaced since early August, approximately
